title: Recipe Card Short Links
story: A recipe site prints a short link on every recipe card, like rcp.ly/0021, so people can type it into a phone. Behind it is the recipe's row ID in the database, written in base 62 using the digits, lowercase letters and uppercase letters.
This is the core of a URL shortener (see Design a URL Shortener): an ID generator hands out unique numbers (Unique IDs), and base 62 turns each into a short code and back on every redirect.
task: • constructor(width): codes are padded on the left with "0" to at least width characters. A number that needs more characters gets a longer code; it is never cut.
• decode(code): return the number a code stands for. Leading "0" characters add nothing, so "0021" and "21" decode to the same number.

The 62 digits, in order of value from 0 to 61, are 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ. So "a" is 10, "z" is 35, "A" is 36 and "Z" is 61. The number 0 is the single digit "0" before padding.
constraints: 0 ≤ id ≤ 9,007,199,254,740,991 (the largest safe integer in JavaScript)
Every code passed to decode uses only the 62 digits, has 1 to 12 characters, and stands for a number in the same range as id.

examples.explanation: 125 = 2 × 62 + 1, so its base-62 digits are 2 and 1: "21", padded to "0021". Decoding left to right: 0, then 0 × 62 + 0 = 0, then 0 × 62 + 2 = 2, then 2 × 62 + 1 = 125. Without the padding the answer is the same.

125,000,017 needs 5 digits: 8, then s, u, d, j (28, 30, 13, 19), and 8 × 62⁴ + 28 × 62³ + 30 × 62² + 13 × 62 + 19 = 125,000,017. 3,844 is exactly 62², so it is "100", as 100 is 10² in decimal. Putting uppercase before lowercase would give a different code that decodes to a different recipe.

hints: In decimal, how do you get the last digit of 4,071, and what is left after removing it? Base 62 works the same way with 62 in place of 10.
The last base-62 digit of id is id % 62. Divide by 62 (rounding down) and repeat until nothing is left. The digits come out last first, so build the string from the right.
Padding only adds "0" characters on the left. When a number needs more digits than width, keep them all: cutting to width would give two recipes the same link.

To decode, start from 0 and, for each character left to right, multiply by 62 and add the character's value (its position in the alphabet string). A map from character to value makes each lookup O(1).
bruteForce: You could count up through every string in order ("0", "1", …, "Z", "10", …) and keep a table from number to code. The millionth recipe means a million steps or a million stored rows, plus a reverse table for decoding.
Base 62 is a formula both ways, so no table is needed: each direction takes one step per character, and codes here never exceed 12 characters.

tests.note: zero is one digit; 9 and 10 cross from digits to letters
z, A, Z and the first two-digit code
zero padded to full width, and back
ZZ and ZZZ: largest two- and three-digit values
longer than the width: never cut
consecutive IDs give codes that differ only at the end

js: const VALUE = new Map([...DIGITS].map((ch, i) => [ch, i]));
code = DIGITS[id % 62] + code; // last digit first
for (const ch of code) n = n * 62 + VALUE.get(ch);
py: VALUE = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(DIGITS)}
if id == 0:               # checked after: 0 still gives "0"
walkthrough: Base 62 is ordinary place value with 62 symbols instead of 10: each position is worth 62 times the one to its right.
• 125 % 62 = 1, so the last digit is "1". 125 / 62 rounded down is 2.
• 2 % 62 = 2, so the next digit is "2". 2 / 62 rounded down is 0, so the loop stops.
• The digits came out as 1, then 2, so the code is "21". Pad to 4: "0021".
To decode "0021", start with n = 0 and read the characters from left to right. The first two zeros leave n at 0, the digit 2 gives 0 × 62 + 2 = 2, and the digit 1 gives 2 × 62 + 1 = 125.

Two details break naive versions. Padding must never cut a code: 238,328 needs 4 digits, "1000", and trimming it to width 3 gives "000", the code for 0. And the alphabet order must match the task exactly: it is a contract between the code that writes links and the code that reads them, and changing it breaks every printed card.
solution.timeWhy: Both directions do one step per character, and a code has L ≤ 12 characters.
solution.spaceWhy: The only extra storage is the code being built, and the alphabet map has a fixed 62 entries.
solution.takeaway: A short code is a number written in a larger base. Unique numbers are generated elsewhere and then encoded, and with 62 symbols, 7 characters already cover 62⁷ ≈ 3.5 trillion IDs.
